headline: Progress of Ministry of Civil Aviation under Special Campaign 5.0
fullText:
Ministry of Civil Aviation

Progress of Ministry of Civil Aviation under Special Campaign 5.0

Massive push toward clutter-free workplace, file weeding, and rapid grievance disposal

16 SEP 2026 9:58PM by PIB Delhi

Under the leadership of Minister of Civil Aviation Shri Ram Mohan Naidu, the Ministry has recorded substantial operational progress across all parameters, incorporating Swachhata as a way of life. The Minister conducted continuous digital file reviews and ministerial oversight of citizen grievances via AirSewa and CPGRAMS portals. The Passenger Assistance Control Room was also operationalized by Shri Ram Mohan Naidu on 10.12.2025 for realtime monitoring of aviation operations and swift redressal of passenger grievances, thereby institutionalizing a passenger first governance approach of the government.

The Ministry of Civil Aviation actively participated in the Special Campaign for Disposal of Pending Matters (SCDPM) 5.0 during the period of 1st November, 2025 to 31st August, 2026.

Significant Progress achieved:

A total of 6,803 physical files and 1,316 e-files have been reviewed, out of which 570 e-files were successfully closed.

A total of 1,628 physical files have been successfully weeded out.

A total of 1,166 cleanliness campaigns have successfully been conducted.

Approximately 18,308 sq. ft. of office space has been freed through disposal of scrap, e-waste and redundant files.

A revenue of Rs. 41,20,582 has been generated as a result of scrap disposal.

Over 7,250 Public Grievances and 2,100 grievance appeals have been successfully resolved during the period, achieving a grievance redressal rate of approximately 99%.

The Ministry actively cleared pending inter-ministerial communications, disposing of 41 MP References, 20 PMO References, 3 IMC References and 14 State Government References in the said period.

The Ministry continues its unwavering commitment to fostering a positive, responsive, and clutter-free workplace, keeping passenger centricity at its core.

headline: Nation gears up for Swachhata Hi Seva 2026
fullText:
Ministry of Jal Shakti

Nation gears up for Swachhata Hi Seva 2026

Union Ministers Shri C. R. Paatil, Shri Tokhan Sahu and Shri V. Somanna call for nationwide participation in Swachhata Hi Seva 2026

SHS 2026 campaign places students and youth at the heart of sustained behaviour change for Swachhata

‘Swachhata Mein Sahbhag; Swachh Bharat, Viksit Bharat’ announced as the theme of SHS 2026

16 SEP 2026 9:57PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Jal Shakti, Shri C. R. Patil, Union Minister of State for Housing and Urban Affairs, Shri Tokhan Sahu addressed a curtain-raiser media interaction for Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 at the National Media Centre in New Delhi today.

Observed annually since 2017, Swachhata Hi Seva 2026, beginning from 17th September this year, brings citizens, institutions and leadership together to strengthen voluntarism and collective action for Swachhata. The SHS 2026 theme, ‘Swachhata Mein Sahbhag; Swachh Bharat, Viksit Bharat’, underlines that Swachhata is a shared responsibility and that the vision of a Swachh and Viksit Bharat can be realized only through the active participation of all citizens.

The national curtain-raiser event/ interaction was held ahead of the nationwide campaign beginning tomorrow. Jointly organized by the Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation (DDWS), Ministry of Jal Shakti and Department of Urban Development (DoUD) Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, SHS 2026 will bring together Central Ministries and Departments, States/UTs Rural and Urban local bodies, institutions and other stakeholders for collective action for Swachhata.

Speaking on the occasion, Union Minister of Jal Shakti, Shri C R Patil, underscored that, under the visionary leadership of the Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, Swachhata has evolved into a national movement driven by Jan Bhagidari. He noted that the Hon’ble Prime Minister has consistently led this movement from the front and inspired citizens across the country. Emphasizing that cleanliness is a shared responsibility, he called upon every citizen, particularly students and youth, to participate wholeheartedly in SHS 2026 and strengthen the collective resolve for a Swachh Bharat and Viksit Bharat. The Minister cited the example of Navsari’s ‘Swachhata Se Swagat’- Micro Swachhata Abhiyaan before the visit of Hon’ble Prime Minister, where people from all walks of life came together for micro cleaning in villages. He also referred to the example of Surat for prompt cleaning after Visarjan of Ganpati last year and people coming together for support, recognition and felicitation of sanitation workers. He mentioned that people are now increasingly coming out to participate and contribute to Swachhata which is the awareness and behaviour change brought about by the Hon’ble Prime Minister in the country.

In a virtual message, Union Minister for Housing and Urban Affairs, Shri Manohar Lal, called upon States to ensure enthusiastic participation in the upcoming Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 campaign. He requested that citizens begin the campaign by cleaning their own homes on 17th September. He further requested that all Ministers, MLAs, Mayors, Deputy Mayors, Ward Councillors, Commissioners and eminent personalities of the State should participate in Nation-wide shramdaan on 1st October. He also urged that cleanliness activities at public places be organized on 2nd October, or Swachh Bharat Diwas, in remembrance of Mahatma Gandhi. He also appealed to students and youth, sportspersons, artists, spiritual leaders, and other Swachhata ambassadors to use their platforms to encourage wider public participation and collective action at the grassroots.

Addressing the gathering, Union Minister of State for Housing and Urban Affairs, Shri Tokhan Sahu said, “The message of swachhata will be effective only when our government offices and institutions themselves set the example. All departments must ensure visible cleanliness in their offices, premises, and subordinate units, along with citizen mobilization, so that this campaign becomes a powerful demonstration of participation —a ‘Whole of Government’ and a ‘Whole of Society’ approach. Every Urban Local Body, Gram Panchayat, every ward, every institution, every community, must be connected with this campaign, making cleanliness a shared national resolve.”

The Secretaries of the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation and the Department of Urban Development highlighted the campaign framework.

The five key pillars of SHS 2026 are:

Transformation of Cleanliness Target Units (CTUs) & Clean Public Places: Identification, mapping and time-bound transformation of difficult and dirty spots, along with cleanliness drives at CTUs and high-footfall public places.

Swachh Paathshala- Yuva for Swachhata: Engagement of students and youth through ‘Swachhata Gyan Yatra’ exposure visits to solid waste management facilities and ‘Swachhata Evam Jal Sanchay Samvad’ covering Swachhata, rainwater harvesting and water management.

SafaiMitra Suraksha Evam Samman Shivir: Single-window camps facilitating health check-ups, PPE and safety gear, and linkages with eligible Central and State welfare schemes. Safai Mitras, Swachhagrahis and sanitation workers will also be felicitated locally in recognition of their contribution for Swachhata.

Jan Bhagidari for Swachhata: Citizen engagement, awareness on the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 and 4-way source segregation and composting. Activities will also include Sports for Swachhata; Swachh Parv, Harit Parv; plantation drives under ‘Ek Ped Maa ke Naam’; World Tourism Day activities (27thSeptember, 2026); and Special Gram Sabhas and Council Meetings on Swachh Bharat Diwas (2ndOctober, 2026).

Swachhata se Samriddhi: Promotion of circularity through ‘Waste to Wealth’, and Waste to Art’; donation and RRR initiatives for old books, toys and clothes, and Plastic Recycling Melas involving Bulk Waste Generators.

Recognizing children and youth as change-makers and the future custodians of Swachh Bharat, SHS 2026 envisages their active involvement through Swachh Paathshala- Yuva for Swachhata in building sustained habits for cleanliness, Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 and four-way source segregation. Initiatives like Sports for Swachhata envisages using local and regional sports to engage children, youth and communities for carrying Swachhata into schools, institutions, cities and villages.

A simultaneous nationwide shramdaan, ‘Ek Din, Ek Ghanta, Ek Saath’, will be organized on 1st October 2026 from 8-9 AM. This will have citizens from different walks of life come together to contribute one hour of voluntary Swachhata service.

On 2nd October 2026, observed as Swachh Bharat Diwas, Special Gram Sabhas will be organized in rural areas, and Special Council Meetings will be organized in urban areas. The Special Gram Sabhas will, among other aspects, focus on outcomes of SHS 2026 and awareness on SWM Rules, 2026. The Swachh Seva Aankalan launched by DDWS for rural areas on 15th September 2026 will also be discussed during the Special Gram Sabhas. Both cities and villages will conduct plantation drives on this day under ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’. On this day Swachhata Pledge will also be voluntarily taken by citizens across the country through MyGov platform.

The SHS 2026 theme, logo, campaign brochure and portal were launched during the event along with SHS 2026 anthem. A curtain raiser video on SHS 2026 was also shown.

Through widespread Jan Bhagidari, SHS 2026 seeks to reinforce Swachhata as a shared responsibility and translate citizen participation into sustained action towards a Swachh and Viksit Bharat. Citizens and participating organizations are encouraged to undertake and share their activities using the hashtags #SHS2026 and #SwachhataHiSeva2026.

(Release ID: 2311161)

headline: On PM Modi’s Directions, Shivraj Singh Chouhan Reaches Bihar to Assess Flood Damage and Crop Loss
fullText:
Ministry of Agriculture &

On PM Modi’s Directions, Shivraj Singh Chouhan Reaches Bihar to Assess Flood Damage and Crop Loss

Shivraj Singh Chouhan Surveys Flood-Hit Bihar with CM Samrat Choudhary, Assesses Damage on Ground

From Hajipur to Bhagalpur and Munger, Shivraj Singh Chouhan Reaches Flood Victims and Reviews Relief Efforts

Union Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan Takes Stock of Flood Crisis in Bihar, Assures Full Central Support

Shivraj Singh Chouhan Reaches Ground Zero by Boat, Tractor and Helicopter, Assures Flood Victims: “We Stand With You”

Banana and Maize Crops Submerged, Millions Affected; Centre and State to Provide All Possible Support: Shivraj Singh Chouhan

Centre Stands Firmly with Every Farmer and Flood Victim in Bihar, Concrete Steps to Follow for Relief and Rehabilitation: Shivraj Singh Chouhan

Bihar Flood Crisis: Centre to Extend Full Support for Relief, Crop Compensation and Rehabilitation, Says Shivraj Singh Chouhan

16 SEP 2026 8:12PM by PIB Patna

Union Agriculture & Farmers’ Welfare and Rural Development Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan today visited flood-affected areas of Bihar on the directions of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and took stock of the situation on the ground. Accompanied by Bihar Chief Minister Shri Samrat Choudhary, state ministers and senior officials from the Centre and the state government, Shri Chouhan conducted an extensive review of the flood situation in Hajipur, Vaishali, Munger and Bhagalpur. He travelled by motorboat, country boat and tractor to reach affected villages and agricultural fields and also conducted an aerial assessment of the situation. Interacting with flood-affected families, he assured them that the Central Government, under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, stands firmly with the people of Bihar and will provide all possible financial and infrastructure support to help the state overcome the crisis.

Central Government Closely Monitoring Flood Situation

The Centre is closely monitoring the flood situation in Bihar following a sharp and, in several areas, record rise in the water levels of the Ganga and other rivers. On the Prime Minister’s directions, Shri Chouhan reached Bihar on Tuesday along with a high-level central team comprising senior officials and technical experts from the Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers’ Welfare, Ministry of Rural Development and various central institutions. After reaching Patna, he began the field assessment along with Chief Minister Shri Samrat Choudhary, members of the state Cabinet and senior administrative officials.

Chouhan Visits Flooded Villages Fields and Relief Camps

In Hajipur, Vaishali, Shri Chouhan visited the worst-affected villages of Terasia and Saraipur, where he travelled by motorboat and country boat to inspect inundated residential areas and agricultural fields. At several difficult-to-reach locations, he travelled by tractor to assess the situation. He also reviewed the extent of flooding and water levels from the Raghopur Six-Lane Bridge. In Munger, the Union Minister inspected the Nawagarhi relief camp and the Kojikaraiya embankment and reviewed arrangements for safety and water drainage. In Bhagalpur, he visited relief camps and interacted with flood-affected people who had taken shelter there.

Water Level Nearly One Foot Higher Than 2016 Floods

After the field visits, Shri Chouhan told the media that, according to information shared by the Chief Minister and local residents, water levels in the affected areas have risen nearly one foot above the levels recorded during the historic floods of 2016. He said banana and maize crops have been severely damaged after remaining submerged for more than 10 days. Nearly 50 lakh people have been directly affected by the floods. Many families have been forced to leave their homes, houses have been damaged and livestock has also been lost. “Seeing farmers’ crops, on which they have invested their hard work and livelihood, submerged in floodwater is deeply painful. But farmers need not lose heart. The government is fully committed to protecting their livelihoods and supporting them through this difficult time,” Shri Chouhan said.

State Government’s Relief and Rescue Efforts Reviewed

Shri Chouhan appreciated the state government’s response to the situation and said that the administration, under the leadership of Chief Minister Shri Samrat Choudhary, is working round the clock on relief and rescue operations. As part of immediate assistance, the state government has begun transferring Rs 7,000 directly into the bank accounts of each affected family through DBT. The process is being carried out on a war footing. Doctors and paramedical teams are being sent by boat to flood-affected areas to provide medical assistance and medicines to people in their homes and at relief camps. Arrangements have also been made for safe shelter, clean drinking water, dry rations and cooked food packets for affected families.

Central Team to Undertake Detailed Damage Assessment

Shri Chouhan said that while the state government is providing immediate assistance through its State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF) and available resources, the Central Government will extend all necessary support for relief, recovery and reconstruction. Officials from the Agriculture and Rural Development departments are conducting a preliminary assessment of the situation. A detailed Inter-Ministerial Central Team will subsequently be sent to Bihar to assess the extent of damage. The team will assess losses across affected districts, particularly damage to agricultural crops, roads, bridges, houses and livestock. Shri Chouhan said that once the state government submits the required proposal under the National Disaster Response Fund, the Centre will provide adequate financial and material assistance without delay.

No Affected Family Will Be Left Helpless

Reassuring flood-affected families, Shri Chouhan said that the Centre and the Prime Minister stand firmly with the people of Bihar. “I assure the people of Bihar, on behalf of the Central Government and Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, that although the crisis is serious, our resolve to serve the people is stronger. We will stand shoulder to shoulder with the state government in helping Bihar overcome this crisis. No affected family will be left helpless,” he said.

High-Level Review Meeting at Chief Minister’s Residence

After the day-long visit to flood-affected areas, embankments and relief camps across the state, Shri Chouhan will chair a high-level review meeting at 6 PM today at the Chief Minister’s residence on Anne Marg. Senior officials from the concerned departments of the Central and state governments will attend the meeting. The review will cover the distribution of relief material, healthcare services, the plan for crop compensation and restoration of damaged infrastructure. Necessary directions will be issued accordingly.

Unproven Stem Cell Interventions, Including Stem Cell Therapy for ASD, Not to be Offered as Routine, Standard or Commercial Clinical Services

17 SEP 2026 9:18AM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Health & Family Welfare has issued an advisory dated 16 September 2026 to all States and Union Territories that have adopted the Clinical Establishments (Registration and Regulation) Act, 2010, regarding regulation of stem cell therapy. The advisory has been issued in view of the judgment dated 30 January 2026 of the Hon’ble Supreme Court in Yash Charitable Trust & Ors. v. Union of India & Ors., W.P. (C) No. 369 of 2022 [2026 INSC 96].

The advisory reiterates the existing framework governing stem cell research and therapy and seeks to ensure that stem cell therapy is permitted as standard care in routine clinical practice only for disease conditions/indications included in the list approved by the Ministry of Health & Family Welfare.

With regard to Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD), the advisory stipulates that the therapeutic use of any type of stem cell in autism is to remain restricted to duly approved clinical trials, in accordance with the National Guidelines for Stem Cell Research, 2017, issued jointly by Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) and the Department of Biotechnology (DBT) and other applicable Government instructions issued by the Government of India from time to time.

The Ministry has requested the States and Union Territories to widely disseminate the directions of the Hon’ble Supreme Court to all concerned State and District Regulatory Authorities and Government and private clinical establishments involved in stem cell research, treatment, promotion or administration, for strict compliance with the applicable framework.

The advisory also draws attention to the consequences of non-compliance with the framework governing stem cell therapy. The Hon’ble Supreme Court, in Para 151(xiii) of its judgment dated 30 January 2026, held that non-compliance with the statutory mandate must attract consequences, including professional misconduct under Regulation 7.22 of the IMC Regulations, 2002, as well as action under Sections 32 and 40 of the Clinical Establishments (Registration and Regulation) Act, 2010, which provide for cancellation of registration and penalty.

The Ministry has accordingly requested the concerned State and District Regulatory Authorities and clinical establishments to ensure strict compliance with the applicable framework governing stem cell research and therapy.

Reinforcing the regulatory position, the National Medical Commission (NMC), in its advisory dated 5 September 2026, reiterated that stem cell therapy may be offered as standard clinical care only for the approved indications. The advisory further states that unauthorised administration, prescription, promotion or advertisement of stem cell therapy beyond the approved indications would constitute to professional misconduct.

The NMC has further advised State Medical Councils to examine cases of alleged violations brought to their notice and, where professional misconduct by a Registered Medical Practitioner is established after due process, take appropriate disciplinary action in accordance with the applicable statutory and regulatory provisions.

headline: Ministry of Coal urges Uttar Pradesh to Expedite Development of its Captive Coal Block; CIL Remains Committed to Meeting the State's Coal Requirement

Ministry of Coal

Ministry of Coal urges Uttar Pradesh to Expedite Development of its Captive Coal Block; CIL Remains Committed to Meeting the State's Coal Requirement

Saharpur Jamarpani block, holding reserves of over 973 million tonnes, remains unoperational more than a decade after allotment; UPRVUNL's coal stock continues to build up on the back of sustained CIL supplies

17 SEP 2026 8:51AM by PIB Delhi

Recent media reports have indicated that the State of Uttar Pradesh is facing a severe power shortage on account of a disruption in coal supply. The Ministry of Coal places the following facts on record to clarify the actual position and to reiterate its advice to the State to expedite development of its own captive coal block, even as Coal India Limited (CIL) continues to fully meet the State's coal requirement.

As on 15.09.2026, none of the thermal power plants of Uttar Pradesh Rajya Vidyut Utpadan Nigam Limited (UPRVUNL) is in the critical-stock category. The current stock position, therefore, does not indicate any critical coal availability constraint at the plant end.

UP Needs to Expedite Development of Its Own Captive Mine

The Saharpur Jamarpani coal block in Dumka district, Jharkhand, holding reserves of more than 973 million tonnes, was allotted to UPRVUNL by the Ministry of Coal on 13.08.2015 under the Coal Mines (Special Provisions) Act, 2015, specifically to meet the coal requirement of UPRVUNL's thermal power projects.

More than ten years since the allotment, no progress has been made towards operationalisation of the block, on account of a lack of requisite initiative by UPRVUNL. As a result, the entire coal requirement of Uttar Pradesh's power plants continues to be met by CIL.

By contrast, fourteen other coal blocks allotted for captive use in the power sector on or after the date of allotment of Saharpur Jamarpani have already been operationalised and have commenced coal production for their respective end-use plants. The Ministry of Coal has advised the State of Uttar Pradesh to take urgent steps towards development of the Saharpur Jamarpani block, so as to reduce its dependence on external sources and secure long-term fuel security for its power plants.

Coal Supply Position: CIL Continues to Fully Support UPRVUNL

The coal stock position at UPRVUNL's thermal power plants has been improving steadily. Stock stood at 7.25 lakh tonnes (LT) on 01.09.2026 and rose to 8.41 LT by 15.09.2026. Over the last seven days, average daily coal receipt of around 0.90 LT has exceeded average daily consumption of around 0.83 LT, reflecting a continuing build-up of stock.

Coal stock at UPRVUNL plants (LT) | 7.25 | 8.41

This improvement is also reflected in sustained rail supplies: over the last 10 days, CIL supplied an average of around 17.7 rakes/day to UPRVUNL's power plants. CIL has additionally offered extra quantities under Road/RCR mode to all Gencos/IPPs, including UPRVUNL, on 03.09.2026, to further build up stock at thermal power plants (TPPs).

Issues requiring attention at UPRVUNL Plants

Unloading constraints at various plants, which lead to periodic restrictions on rake placement by the Railways, limiting further augmentation of coal supplies.

It is also pertinent to note that despite coal stock having increased to over 8 LT, the current-month Plant Load Factor (PLF) of UPRVUNL's thermal power plants stands at only around 48%. The lower generation during the current month cannot, therefore, be attributed to inadequate coal availability at the plant end. Improvement in generation would require the State to address operational constraints at its generating stations and ensure optimal utilisation of available coal stock.

The Ministry of Coal and Coal India Limited remain fully committed to supplying coal to the entire country, including the State of Uttar Pradesh. At the same time, the Ministry advises the State of Uttar Pradesh to accord priority to the early development of its captive coal block at Saharpur Jamarpani, so as to build long-term fuel security for its thermal power plants and reduce dependence on external coal sources.

Vice President Pays Tribute to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel and the Heroes of the Hyderabad Liberation Struggle at the Hyderabad Liberation Day Celebrations

Hyderabad Liberation marks a significant chapter in the nation’s journey: Vice President

Firm resolve of Sardar Patel, courage of armed forces and struggle of people of Hyderabad strengthened national unity: Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat

17 SEP 2026 4:22PM by PIB Delhi

At a grand ceremony held today at Secunderabad Parade Ground on the occasion of Hyderabad Liberation Day, Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan recalled the historic chapter of the integration of the erstwhile princely state of Hyderabad into India and paid tribute to all the heroes who fought for the unity and integrity of the nation.

Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said that the story of Hyderabad is, in many ways, the story of the making of India. He added that the integration of the erstwhile princely state of Hyderabad into a unified India on September 17, 1948, marked a significant chapter in the nation’s journey of nation-building. He noted that it was part of the journey of national unity and nation-building that strengthened the foundations of modern India. He also recalled and paid homage to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel for his decisive role in the integration of the princely states.

Union Minister of Culture and Tourism Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, while paying tribute to the martyrs, said that it was the firm resolve of Iron Man Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, the indomitable courage of the armed forces, and the unwavering desire of the people of Hyderabad to merge with India, coupled with their struggle, that brought the region into the fold of national unity. He also highlighted the contribution of the brave soldiers of the Jodhpur Lancers in this struggle.

Union Minister of State for Home Affairs Shri Bandi Sanjay Kumar said that the people of Hyderabad had suffered under the Nizam’s rule and the atrocities committed by the Razakars. He said that Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, with firm resolve, freed them from this tyranny and made Hyderabad an integral part of India.

At the ceremony, 10 contingents of the Central Armed Police Forces presented a march past. The historical and cultural context of Hyderabad was presented through a special cultural performance on the theme “Hyderabad Vimochanam”. On the occasion, the winners of the Hyderabad Liberation Day Quiz Competition, held at the Salar Jung Museum, were felicitated by the Vice President.

The Vice President visited a special exhibition organised by the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting at the venue, showcasing historical episodes connected with Hyderabad Liberation Day and the journey of national unity.

On the occasion, Telangana Governor Shri Shiv Pratap Shukla, Union Minister of Coal and Mines Shri G. Kishan Reddy, Malkajgiri MP Shri Etala Rajender, Secretary, Ministry of Culture, Shri Vivek Aggarwal, and Director General, Central Reserve Police Force, Shri Gyanendra Pratap Singh, among other dignitaries, were present.

The Hyderabad Liberation Day celebrations, while commemorating a significant chapter of history, also underscored the role of citizens in nation-building, the constitutional values of equality, dignity and opportunity, and the resolve to continuously strengthen India’s unity.

Shivraj Singh Chouhan Plants Saplings with Sarpanches on PM Modi’s Birthday, Also Addresses VB–G RAM G Workshop Held at Delhi

Fraud in Viksit Bharat–G RAM G Scheme Will Not Be Tolerated at Any Cost – Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan

If a Pond Is Already Full and Workers Are Still Being Engaged There, It Is a Matter of Concern; Conduct Random Inspections of Works – Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan

Technology Has Been Used to Leave No Scope for Fraud; Face Authentication-Based Attendance of Workers Made Mandatory – Shivraj Singh Chouhan

Focus on Building Developed Villages While Following the 60% Wage and 40% Material Norm – Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan

Let ViksitGaon Be Built for a Viksit Bharat; the Objective of the Scheme Is Not Merely to Dig Soil and Dump It Elsewhere – Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan

Irregularities of MGNREGA Will Not Be Allowed to Be Repeated Under Viksit Bharat–G RAM G at Any Cost – Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan

17 SEP 2026 4:18PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Rural Development and Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan, today planted saplings with sarpanches and departmental officials at the Pusa campus in New Delhi on the occasion of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s birthday and extended his birthday greetings to the Prime Minister. Thereafter, the Union Minister addressed the National Workshop organised on Viksit Bharat–G RAM G. The workshop was attended by elected representatives of Panchayati Raj Institutions, Commissioners and senior officials of States and Union Territories, and other participants.

On the occasion, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan directed officials to conduct random inspections of works being undertaken under the scheme. Where works are being carried out in accordance with the prescribed standards and procedures, the concerned persons should be appreciated. However, wherever any irregularity is found, strict action should be taken at the very outset so that no one dares to violate the rules in future.

There Will Be No Leniency in Case of Fraud

Union Minister for Rural Development Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan issued a strong message to the States and Union Territories regarding any kind of fraud and irregularity under the Viksit Bharat–G RAM G Scheme. He said that fraud in the scheme would not be tolerated at any cost.

Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan said, “Remember, we will not allow any fraud in this scheme at any cost. I am clearly saying as the Minister that if there is any fraud, no one will be spared. Action will be taken against anyone who indulges in irregularities.” He said that if a pond in a village is already full and workers are still being engaged there, it is a matter that needs to be investigated. He directed officials to keep a close watch on such cases.

Conduct Random Inspections of Works; Take Action at the Very Outset if Irregularities Are Found

Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan told officials of States and Union Territories that only two months have passed since the scheme was launched and the third month is underway. Therefore, it is essential to keep the monitoring and inspection mechanism strong right from the beginning. He directed that random inspections of selected works be conducted. Where works are being carried out properly, the concerned persons should be appreciated, while any irregularity found should invite immediate action so that irregularities are curbed at the initial stage and such situations do not recur in future.

Technology Will Help Curb Fraud

The Union Minister said that technology has been used in the scheme to ensure better monitoring of works and to leave no scope for fraud. He said that attendance of workers has now been made mandatory through Face Authentication. Therefore, it should also be ensured through the technological system that there are no gaps in this mechanism.

He said that when a complaint comes to light, it is natural to be concerned. He urged all concerned officials to ensure that no breach occurs at any level in the implementation of the scheme. He said, “All the officials are sitting here, and I want to tell them and the Commissioners to ensure that no one is able to breach the system at any cost.”

Ensure Work for Workers; They Should Not Remain Without Work Even for an Hour

Union Minister for Rural Development Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan said that the most important objective of the scheme is to provide employment to workers. He said that workers should get work and should not remain without work even for an hour. He also emphasised that timely payment of wages must be ensured. He said that works permitted under the rules should be undertaken after following the prescribed procedures.

He also emphasised adherence to the wage-material ratio under the scheme. He said that at the district level, 60 per cent of the funds are to be spent on wages and 40 per cent on material. Officials were directed to follow the rules and prescribed procedures and prioritise works that create durable and useful assets in villages.

Work Does Not Mean Merely Digging Soil and Dumping It Elsewhere

The Union Minister said that work does not mean merely digging soil at one place and dumping it at another. Keeping in view the objective of “ViksitGaon for a Viksit Bharat”, works under the Viksit Bharat–G RAM G Scheme should be considered in a manner that creates a strong foundation for development in villages and strengthens the rural economy.

He told officials that there is now a need to consider how the Viksit Bharat–G RAM G Scheme can contribute to building ViksitGaon. Along with providing employment, the scheme should facilitate the creation of assets that remain useful to rural communities over the long term and help make villages self-reliant and developed.

Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan said that the success of the scheme can be ensured only when workers receive adequate employment, transparency is maintained in the execution of works, fraud is completely curbed, and the scheme also contributes to building developed villages alongside a developed India.

National Service Is the Core Mantra of PM Modi’s Life

Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan said that today is a highly relevant and special day. There is an atmosphere of joy and celebration across the country. Today is the birthday of our Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi. On this occasion, he extended heartfelt greetings and best wishes to the Prime Minister on behalf of rural India.

He said, “My only prayer to God is that Prime Minister Narendra Modi ji may be blessed with a long and healthy life and may he continue to serve the country and its people in the same manner.” He said that national service has remained the core mantra of the Prime Minister’s life.

He said that his journey of public service as the head of government for 25 consecutive years is significant in itself. He served as the Chief Minister of Gujarat and is now leading the nation as the Prime Minister. This long and continuous journey of service is a noteworthy chapter in the history of Indian democracy.

He said that under the leadership of the Prime Minister, the vision of a new India is taking shape—an India that is prosperous, glorious, strong, self-reliant and developed.

fullText:
Ministry of Road Transport & Highways

NHAI Rajmargyatra App Hosts ‘OneTag’ FASTag Portability Service

Availability of ‘OneTag’ FASTag portability has expanded the citizen centric services available for National Highway users on Rajmargyatra Mobile App

17 SEP 2026 4:15PM by PIB Delhi

In order to enhance consumer choice for FASTag users, ‘OneTag’ - a FASTag portability service is now available on National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) Rajmargyatra App. The initiative enables FASTag users to change their issuer while retaining the existing FASTag affixed to their vehicle, eliminating the need to obtain a new physical tag. The availability of ‘OneTag’ FASTag portability has expanded citizen centric services available for National Highway users on Rajmargyatra App, which include FASTag Annual Pass, FASTag Local Pass, Emergency Helpline 1033 among other services.

The Rajmargyatra app guides users through the FASTag portability process. FASTag users can login to App and enter their vehicle registration number to check eligibility. The user will receive a verification six-digit Mobile Verification Code (MVC) from current issuer bank. Following authorization, the user will be required to select a new issuer, complete customer verification and wallet onboarding with the new issuer to complete the portability process. Following successful portability, the existing FASTag ID linked to vehicle registration number will remain unchanged, allowing users to continue using the same physical tag with a different issuer bank.

After portability is completed, previous issuer will close the existing FASTag wallet and refund the available balance, post applicable adjustments. Also, interoperable FASTag has a cooling period of 6 months before it can be ported again.

The ‘OneTag’ initiative will help to improve FASTag lifecycle management by reducing the need for repeated tag production, thereby lowering operational costs, dispatching and reissuance expenses. ‘OneTag’ will also help to streamline the issuer-switching journey, enhance customer choice and contribute to a more interoperable and efficient FASTag ecosystem.

With a penetration rate of over 98 percent and around 13 crore users, FASTag has revolutionized the Electronic Toll Collection system in the country. The introduction of ‘OneTag’ will further strengthen the digital tolling architecture and provide FASTag users with greater flexibility, while retaining the existing physical tag and proving greater convenience to the National Highway users.

headline: S&T based community initiative improves detection and control of TB in Rajasthan
fullText:
Ministry of Science & Technology

S&T based community initiative improves detection and control of TB in Rajasthan

17 SEP 2026 3:32PM by PIB Delhi

A new, scientific data-based community driven initiative has dramatically improved TB detection and control in remote, underserved regions of Rajasthan.

Tuberculosis continues to be a major public health problem in many remote areas like the tribal districts of Rajasthan. Factors such as difficult terrain, low awareness, social stigma, seasonal migration, and delayed diagnosis have long hindered TB control efforts and led to TB burden.

In order to address this, AIIMS Jodhpur conducted Cluster based population survey, active case finding, laboratory confirmation to estimate the burden of TB (Active and Latent) among the tribal population and their anti-TB drug resistance pattern.

The study has found ways to limit transmission of TB in the tribal districts of southern Rajasthan, through early detection and streamlining patients to undergo preventive screening through community participation and reaching out with timely treatment.

Fig: Filed work- screening, sputum collection, Transport and health awareness

With support from the SEED division of the Department of Science and Technology (DST), they conducted Household survey, symptom screening, sputum testing, NTEP diagnostics and data analysis among more than 6000 people from Sirohi, Udaipur, Chittorgarh, Dungarpur, Pratapgarh and Banswara districts.

The researchers led by Dr Shoban Babu Varthya (Additional Professor), Department of Pharmacology AIIMS Jodhpur conducted workshops to sensitize people and combined epidemiological survey, grass root level participation of Healthcare workers (HCWs) and panchayat people to improve early detection. Active case finding laboratory confirmation was also undertaken.

People with symptoms of tuberculosis and those with positive results were identified and given treatment for TB as per national guidelines. Besides, community awareness was generated to improve the understanding of TB to help limit the transmission of TB through early detection and streamlining patients to undergo preventive screening among household contacts. This helped enable implementation of TB Mukt Panchayat model with the use of scientific data.

This initiative demonstrates how targeted, scientific research can generate actionable data that directly informs policy and strengthens TB control in vulnerable populations.

(Release ID: 2311342)
summaryText:
### OVERVIEW
A science and technology-based community initiative, supported by the Department of Science and Technology and led by AIIMS Jodhpur, has successfully improved the early detection and control of tuberculosis (TB) in remote tribal districts of Rajasthan.

### KEY HIGHLIGHTS
* **Research Leadership:** Led by Dr. Shoban Babu Varthya, Additional Professor, Department of Pharmacology, AIIMS Jodhpur.
* **Supporting Agency:** The SEED division of the Department of Science and Technology (DST).
* **Scale and Locations:** Conducted household surveys, symptom screening, sputum testing, and diagnostics among more than 6,000 people across six districts: Sirohi, Udaipur, Chittorgarh, Dungarpur, Pratapgarh, and Banswara.
* **Methodology:** Utilized cluster-based population surveys, active case finding, laboratory confirmation, NTEP diagnostics, and data analysis to estimate the burden of active and latent TB and assess anti-TB drug resistance patterns.
* **Community Engagement:** Conducted workshops to sensitize the public and integrated grassroots participation from healthcare workers (HCWs) and panchayat members to improve early detection and generate awareness.
* **Interventions and Outcomes:** Identified and treated symptomatic individuals per national guidelines, streamlined patients for preventive screening among household contacts, and successfully enabled the implementation of the "TB Mukt Panchayat" model using scientific data.

- Direct bank transfers implemented swiftly after the new government took office, with strict elimination of corrupt practices.

बांग्लार आमार मां बोनेदेर आमार प्रोणाम ओ शुभेक्छा!

आज इस विशेष अवसर पर आप सभी से जुड़कर मुझे बहुत खुशी हो रही है। बंगाल की माताओं-बहनों से मुझे हमेशा बहुत स्नेह मिला है। आपका विश्वास और अपनापन, मेरे लिए बहुत बड़ी शक्ति है। आपनार भरोशा आमार शोक्ति !!!

आज विश्वकर्मा पूजा का पावन अवसर भी है। मैं आप सभी को विश्वकर्मा पूजा की बहुत-बहुत शुभकामनाएं देता हूं।

इसी पावन समय में, आज बंगाल में एक नई परंपरा सशक्त हो रही है। आज अन्नपूर्णा योजना के रूप में बंगाल की माताओं-बहनों से नया सामर्थ्य जुड़ा है। मैं इस योजना से लाभ पाने वाली हर बहन को बधाई देता हूं, अपनी शुभकामनाएं देता हूं।

घर में हमारी माताओं-बहनों के कंधों पर बहुत सारी जिम्मेदारियां होती हैं। अनेक छोटे-बड़े फैसलों के बीच एक महिला हर तरीके से परिवार का ख्याल रखती है और जब उनके पास जरूरी खर्चों की चिंता कम होती है, तो उनका आत्मविश्वास भी और बढ़ जाता है। अन्नपूर्णा योजना, बंगाल की महिलाओं के आत्मविश्वास को मजबूती देने का ऐसा ही महत्वपूर्ण प्रयास है। बंगाल की हमारी बहनों के बैंक खातों में हर महीने एक निश्चित राशि पहुंचे। ऐसी राशि, जिसके लिए उन्हें किसी से कहना न पड़े, यह उनके जीवन के लिए बहुत बड़ा संबल है। एटी एकटी बॉड़ो शाहाज्जो !!!

आज करीब डेढ़ करोड़ बहनों के खातों में अन्नपूर्णा योजना की चौथी किस्त पहुंच रही है। यानि हर महीने 3 हजार रुपये। यह किसी मां के लिए बच्चे की पढ़ाई का खर्च हो सकता है। किसी बहन के लिए दवा या घर की जरूरी चीज खरीदने का सहारा हो सकता है।

हमारी सोच है, बंगाल की महिलाओं के पास फैसले की ताकत भी हो और आगे बढ़ने का हौसला भी हो। और इसमें अन्नपूर्णा योजना की बड़ी भूमिका है। मैं अन्नपूर्णा योजना की लाभार्थी सभी माताओं-बहनों को बहुत-बहुत बधाई देता हूं।

इस साल चार मई को बंगाल ने परिवर्तन का एक नया रास्ता चुना और मैं जानता हूं, इस परिवर्तन में सबसे अहम भूमिका बंगाल की माताओं-बहनों की रही है। आपने अपने जीवन में बहुत सी कठिनाइयां देखी हैं। बहुत सी चीजों के लिए इंतजार किया है। इसलिए हमारी नई सरकार के सामने सबसे पहली कसौटी यही रही कि बंगाल की महिलाओं का जीवन आसान हो, उनके जीवन में Ease of Living बढ़े। इसलिए हम जिस मूल मंत्र को लेकर चले, वो है- कोथा कॉम, काज बेशी !

अन्नपूर्णा योजना की शुरुआत इसी सोच के साथ हुई है। सरकार बनने के कुछ ही दिनों के भीतर इस योजना पर काम शुरू हुआ और आज, इतनी बड़ी संख्या में महिलाओं तक सीधे बैंक में पैसा पहुंचना शुरू हो गया है। कोई कट मनी नहीं, कोई बिचौलिया नहीं। एखोन बांग्लाए काटमानी चोले ना !!!

हमारी सरकार का यह भी लक्ष्य है कि एक भी पात्र महिला अन्नपूर्णा योजना के लाभ से वंचित न रहे। इसके लिए भी यहां तेजी से काम हो रहा है।

माताओं-बहनों-बेटियों के जीवन चक्र से जुड़ी हर समस्या का समाधान करना भाजपा की सर्वोच्च प्राथमिकता रही है। गर्भावस्था के दौरान शिशु को पौष्टिक खाना मिले, इसके लिए हमने मातृवंदना योजना चलाई, महिलाओं के बैंक खाते में पैसे भेजने शुरू किए। बेटी को कोख में ही ना समाप्त कर दिया जाए, इसके लिए बेटी बचाओ-बेटी पढ़ाओ जैसे जनआंदोलन शुरू किए। बेटी जब बड़ी होकर स्कूल जाने लगे, तो शौचालय ना होने की वजह से स्कूल ना छोड़े, इसके लिए करोड़ों शौचालय बनाए। बेटी की शिक्षा जारी रहे, इसके लिए सुकन्या समृद्धि योजना में इतना ज्यादा ब्याज दिया। बेटी अगर सैनिक स्कूल जाना चाहे, तो उसके लिए हमने सैनिक स्कूल के द्वार खोल दिए। बेटी बड़ी होकर कुछ अपना काम कर सके, इसके लिए बिना गारंटी लोन देने वाली मुद्रा योजना शुरू की। मां बनने के बाद भी वो अपनी नौकरी जारी रख सके, इसके लिए मातृत्व अवकाश में वृद्धि की। बेटी को गांव में कमाई के नए अवसर मिलें, इसके लिए सेल्फ हेल्प ग्रुप को मिलने वाली सहायता में रिकॉर्ड वृद्धि की गई। बेटी को रसोई में लकड़ी का धुआं ना सहना पड़े, इसके लिए उज्जवला का गैस कनेक्शन दिया। बेटी को पानी के इंतजाम में परेशान ना होना पड़े, इसके लिए हमने हर घर नल से जल देने की योजना शुरू की। बेटी को अंधेरे में ना रहना पड़े, इसके लिए हमने सौभाग्य योजना से मुफ्त बिजली कनेक्शन दिया। बेटी पैसे की कमी की वजह से अपनी बीमारी छिपाए नहीं, इसलिए हमने उसे आयुष्मान कार्ड की ताकत दी। बेटी को बैंकों का लाभ मिले, इसके लिए जनधन योजना के तहत बड़ी संख्या में बैंक खाते खोले। बेटी का घर की संपत्ति पर भी अधिकार हो, इसके लिए पीएम आवास के घरों में उसे संयुक्त भागीदारी दी।

बंगाल के लोगों की एक बड़ी पीड़ा यह भी रही है कि बीते 12 वर्षों में केंद्र की ऐसी कई योजनाओं का लाभ यहां समय पर नहीं पहुंच पाया। इससे गरीब परिवारों को सबसे ज्यादा नुकसान हुआ। अब भाजपा सरकार में इन रुकी हुई योजनाओं को तेज गति से आगे बढ़ाया गया है। जैसे एक उदाहरण पीएम आवास योजना का है। बंगाल में भाजपा सरकार बनने के बाद 50 लाख से ज्यादा ऐसे नए गरीब परिवारों की पहचान की गई है, जिनको पीएम आवास योजना के पक्के घर दिए जाएंगे। पीएम विश्वकर्मा योजना को भी यहां लागू किया गया है। हर लंबित योजना, हर अटकी हुई परियोजना, अब बंगाल में नई गति पकड़ रही है। और इसमें बंगाल की महिलाओं का, यहां के लोगों का आशीर्वाद भाजपा के साथ है। इसीलिए, मैं बहुत विश्वास से कहता हूं, आमरा एकशॉन्गे गोड़बो नोतुन बांग्ला! हम सब मिलकर बनाएंगे नया बंगाल।

देश ने विकसित भारत का संकल्प लिया है। मुझे विश्वास है, बंगाल की माताएं-बहनें विकास की यात्रा को इसी तरह नई गति देंगी। विकसित बंगाल के सामर्थ्य से, विकसित भारत का संकल्प और मजबूत होगा।

आप सभी का स्नेह, आपका आशीर्वाद, हमें निरंतर सेवा की प्रेरणा देता है। एक बार फिर, आप सभी को अन्नपूर्णा दिवस की बहुत-बहुत बधाई। विश्वकर्मा पूजा की बहुत-बहुत शुभकामनाएं! धन्यवाद!

headline: English rendering of PM's speech during the inauguration of SEMICON India 2026
fullText:
Prime Minister's Office

English rendering of PM's speech during the inauguration of SEMICON India 2026

17 SEP 2026 2:19PM by PIB Delhi

Thank you very much.

Union Cabinet colleagues Ashwini Vaishnaw ji, Jitin Prasada ji, all industry leaders, CEOs, delegates, and virtually connected hundreds of universities and institutes - the future of India, my young companions. And here present, the large number of enthusiastic youth, ladies and gentlemen!

This is the fifth edition of Semicon India. I welcome you all. I extend a special welcome to the guests who have come from abroad.

Today is also Vishwakarma Jayanti. I extend my best wishes to all countrymen on Vishwakarma Jayanti. In our tradition, Lord Vishwakarma is considered the symbol of the power of construction and creation. And see the coincidence - Semicon India begins today itself. On one side, our centuries‑old tradition of creation, and on the other side, the technology and vision of the 21st century - this is our inspiration for self‑reliant India, for developed India.

Every citizen is committed to building a developed India. If we look at just the past 15 days - I draw your attention only to 15 days - we can see the direction and speed with which India is moving forward. In this September, just 10 days ago, the Global Fintech Fest was held in Mumbai. There was discussion on inclusive finance through agentic AI, tokenization, and quantum technologies. During the same period, nearly 3,000 kilometers of Dedicated Freight Corridor became fully operational in India. I am talking about September’s 10 days, not long ago. This will speed up freight movement in the country, improve logistics, and give new strength to manufacturing.

In this same period, in this September itself, India’s quarterly GDP report came. And even in this challenging period, India achieved 7.8 percent growth. And during the same time, Japan’s credit rating agency upgraded India’s sovereign rating. And this happened after three decades - nearly 35 years. That means, on one side India’s economy is growing, and on the other side, the world’s trust in India is also increasing.

Another big picture of this trust was seen just three days ago at the BRICS Summit. India successfully hosted this summit. The unanimous adoption of the New Delhi Declaration is another big proof of the world’s trust in India.

Amidst these achievements of India, this Semicon India event has become even more important. Its first edition was in 2022. Since then we meet every year, but every year the subject of our discussion has changed. In the first edition, we talked about policy. In the next editions, the discussion moved forward. We began talking about projects - from signing files to laying foundation stones. Last year we began discussing pilot lines and test chips. How the first samples began to come out of India’s units - this was discussed. And this year, we are talking about commercial production. Now chips are coming out of India’s plants and reaching customers in India and the world. And just now, in Mohali and Surat, commercial production has started in two more plants. I congratulate them as well.

For any country, reaching here in such a short time is not easy. This is not a sector where you set up a factory and the work is done. It takes decades to build technological capabilities. Wherever semiconductor ecosystems have been built in the world, they have been prepared after decades of effort. But India, with your cooperation, has worked simultaneously on chip design, manufacturing, equipment manufacturing, materials ecosystem, testing capability - and has shown success. In this journey, you industry leaders have been the major stakeholders. You are the pillars of India’s success, you are the partners in our journey.

In the semiconductor industry, there is a word - “tape‑out.” This is the day when a chip, after design completion, goes into production. But work does not stop after tape‑out. On that very day, work begins on the next version. And India is doing the same. India has started the second phase of the Semiconductor Mission. The size of our first phase was about 8 billion dollars, while the second phase we have set at 13.5 billion dollars. Moving on the Reform Express, we have made further reforms in this sector. Now international companies can also collaborate with our startups, Indian design companies, and OCI‑owned companies. That means whether it is policies, funds, regulatory frameworks - whatever is needed for the success of your projects, the Government of India is taking every step.

Our effort is that fabless companies grow in India, and intellectual property creation also happens in India. Whether it is making different types of compound semiconductors, making silicon photonics part of the ecosystem, or enabling infrastructure for AI - all this is necessary. And in this direction, we must move forward together. The foundation needed for this has already been prepared. India is also focusing greatly on strengthening supply chains. Many reforms have been made for this. To the leaders of equipment companies present here, I say - do not lag behind in taking advantage of this. For leaders in chemicals, gases, and materials too, golden opportunities await in India. We want the entire ecosystem to grow together. For this, the demand pipeline is also ready. So far, 12 projects have been approved, and in the next phase this scope will expand further.

Another advantage for all of you in India is youth - talented, skilled manpower. Today we have a very large pool of engineering talent. India has thousands of engineering colleges, and every year India produces lakhs of engineers. Once, a gentleman from an American company came to meet me. He said, “If we want to recruit engineers in our country, we call them, and they all fit in one room. But in India, if we call engineers, even a football field is too small.” This is India’s strength.

For chip designing, large‑scale skilling work is underway. Just before coming here, I met some young companions from industry on this very campus - all students. These students gifted me chips they had designed themselves. Our government has set a target to train one lakh engineering students for the semiconductor industry. And as you were told, we have already trained more than 70,000 youth. Such a large talent pool is nothing less than a gold mine for all of you.

Amidst these government efforts, today I also appeal to the youth - young talents who are doing research in India should come forward. Those youth who are doing research abroad should also connect with the development of advanced technologies in India. I urge industry leaders to lead R&D in the country. This benefits industry, and it also strengthens India’s youth power.

The advancing semiconductor industry also faces some challenges, which you are all familiar with. For years, people in your industry talked about transistor size. As transistors became smaller, computing became faster and more efficient. Even today this question is important. But now, with the arrival of Artificial Intelligence, some new questions have arisen before this industry. In the past two years, the global semiconductor market has grown by more than 20 percent. And a very big part of this growth is due to demand created by AI. That means, today if you are working on AI, the challenges are not only about what is inside the chip, but also about what is happening around it. Bringing memory closer to the processor, connecting many chips in such a way that they work together as one system, transferring huge amounts of data from here to there without delay, managing heat and power - these are many challenges before the semiconductor industry. Amidst these challenges, the world most needs new and reliable manufacturing locations. And India - I assure you - India is continuously preparing itself for this.

Another major issue before today’s semiconductor industry is energy security. The chips being made for AI are used in AI data centers. In these data centers, thousands of high‑performance processors work together, processing huge amounts of data. As AI expands, the need for computing power will increase at the same pace. And as computing power increases, the need for electricity will also increase greatly. Therefore, investment in the power sector is very important. Where our plants are located, electricity must be available on time, in the required quantity when needed - this is very important. That is why India is making very large investments in the power sector today. In the past decade, our installed solar energy capacity has increased from about 2 gigawatts to more than 160 gigawatts - from 2 to 160. In nuclear energy too, we are moving forward rapidly. This sector has been opened to private players. We are also working on small modular reactors. In the past decade, India has also expanded its transmission network.

This expansion of power infrastructure in India is also a great strength for our semiconductor ecosystem. India is taking every step needed to make itself a preferred destination for the semiconductor industry.

India is the Mother of Democracy. Just a few years ago, our Constitution completed 75 years. When such a country succeeds in a critical industry, it strengthens the entire world’s supply chain. And today, when supply chains are being weaponized, its importance increases even more. We must see the developments happening in India from this larger perspective. India’s aspirations are before you, and the new opportunities being created in India are ready to welcome you. Once again, I extend many congratulations to all of you for this event.

headline: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi inaugurates SEMICON India 2026
fullText:
Prime Minister's Office

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi inaugurates SEMICON India 2026

India's semiconductor ecosystem is expanding rapidly; It is opening new opportunities for innovation, investment and growth: PM

India's economy is growing; the world's trust in India is also growing: PM

Young talents who are researching in India should come forward; The youth who are researching abroad should also join the development of advanced technologies in India: PM

I urge industry leaders to spearhead R&D in the country; This will be mutually beneficial, driving industry growth while empowering India's youth: PM

The world is looking for new and trusted manufacturing destinations; India is steadily preparing itself to meet this need: PM

India is taking every step needed to become a preferred destination for the semiconductor industry: PM

17 SEP 2026 2:04PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today inaugurated SEMICON India 2026 in New Delhi. Addressing the occasion and highlighting the significance of the event's fifth edition, the Prime Minister extended warm greetings to all participants. He expressed particular gratitude to the international attendees who had traveled to India to partake in the summit. "I extend a special welcome to the guests who have come to India from abroad," remarked Shri Modi.

Drawing a powerful parallel between the launch of Semicon India and Vishwakarma Diwas, the Prime Minister honored the nation's centuries-old heritage of construction and creation. He pointed out the beautiful coincidence of merging traditional creative power with 21st-century technology and vision. "This is our inspiration for a self-reliant India, a Viksit Bharat,” asserted Shri Modi.

Emphasizing the nation's rapid progress over the past 15 days, the Prime Minister listed major milestones, including discussions on inclusive finance at the Global Fintech Fest, the operationalization of a 3,000-kilometer Dedicated Freight Corridor, and a robust 7.8 percent quarterly GDP growth. He also highlighted the recent sovereign rating upgrade by a Japanese Credit Rating Agency as a testament to the nation's soaring economic credibility. "Meaning, on one hand, India's economy is growing, and on the other hand, the world's trust in India is also increasing,” observed Shri Modi.

Recalling the diplomatic triumph of the recently concluded BRICS Summit hosted by India, the Prime Minister pointed to the unanimous adoption of the New Delhi Declaration as a reflection of international consensus. He underscored that this historic diplomatic achievement validates the global community's unwavering faith in the nation. "This is another major proof of the world's trust in India,” noted Shri Modi.

Tracing the evolutionary journey of Semicon India since its inception in 2022, the Prime Minister mapped the progression from initial policy discussions to project planning, pilot lines, and finally, the commencement of commercial production. He celebrated the realization of these efforts with chips now reaching global customers, alongside the launch of commercial production in two new plants in Mohali and Surat. "Now our chips, coming out of India's plants, have started reaching customers in the country and the world,” noted Shri Modi.

Acknowledging the immense complexity of building a semiconductor ecosystem, the Prime Minister praised the collaborative effort required to master chip design, equipment manufacturing, and testing capabilities in record time. He credited the present industry leaders as foundational pillars whose partnership made this rapid technological leap possible. "You are the pillars of this success of India, you are partners,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Outlining the relentless momentum of the sector, the Prime Minister explained the concept of 'tape out' and how the government continuously pushes for the next technological version without pause. He announced the massive 13.5 billion dollar second phase of the Semiconductor Mission and highlighted new regulatory reforms that facilitate collaborations between international companies, startups, and design firms. "The Government of India is taking every step needed for the success of your projects,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Detailing the vision for a robust domestic supply chain, the Prime Minister stressed the importance of nurturing fabless companies, creating intellectual property, and integrating silicon photonics for AI-enabling infrastructure. He urged leaders in equipment, chemicals, gases, and materials to capitalize on the golden opportunities presented by the twelve approved projects and an expanding demand pipeline. "We want the entire ecosystem to grow together,” asserted Shri Modi.

Highlighting the strategic advantage of India's demographic dividend, the Prime Minister spoke of the vast pool of engineering talent and the extensive skilling initiatives specifically tailored for chip designing. He proudly mentioned receiving custom-designed chips from students and reiterated the government's ambitious target to train one lakh engineering students, with 70,000 already trained. "Such a large talent pool is, in a way, nothing less than a gold mine for all of you,” remarked Shri Modi.

Calling upon the brilliant minds engaged in domestic and international research, the Prime Minister urged young talents to actively participate in developing advanced technologies within the country. He challenged industry leaders to spearhead local research and development, ensuring mutual growth for both businesses and the nation's youth. "There is benefit for the industry in this, and the youth power of India will also get strength from this,” asserted Shri Modi.

Addressing the evolving complexities of the semiconductor market, the Prime Minister discussed how the explosive demand for Artificial Intelligence is shifting the focus from mere transistor size to holistic system integration, including memory placement and heat management. He positioned the nation as a reliable and continuously prepared destination to meet these new global manufacturing challenges. "India is constantly preparing itself for this,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Tackling the critical issue of energy security for high-performance computing, the Prime Minister outlined the massive power requirements generated by AI data centers and the necessity of uninterrupted electricity for manufacturing plants. He detailed the nation's aggressive expansion in the power sector, including a leap to over 160 GW in solar capacity, the opening of nuclear energy to private players, and the development of small modular reactors. "Therefore, India today is making huge investments in the power sector as well,” noted Shri Modi.

Connecting the rapid expansion of power infrastructure to industrial readiness, the Prime Minister declared that this energy security acts as a fundamental strength for the semiconductor ecosystem. He reassured stakeholders that the administration is deeply committed to optimizing conditions for industrial growth. "India is taking every step that makes us a preferred destination for the semiconductor industry,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Concluding his address by contextualizing the nation's technological strides within its democratic ethos, the Prime Minister reminded the audience of the 75-year legacy of the Indian Constitution. He expressed that a successful critical industry in the 'Mother of Democracy' intrinsically fortifies the entire global supply chain, extending a warm invitation to explore the boundless opportunities ahead. "India's aspirations are before you, and the new opportunities being created in India are ready to welcome you,” affirmed Shri Modi.'

headline: Department of Social Justice and Empowerment Observes ‘SWACHHATA HI SEVA’ Campaign 2026
fullText:

Department of Social Justice and Empowerment Observes ‘SWACHHATA HI SEVA’ Campaign 2026

Secretary SJE Administers Swachhata Pledge To Officers And Officials

‘Swachhata Hi Seva’ Campaign To Conclude On 2nd October 2026

17 SEP 2026 2:01PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Social Justice and Empowerment under Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, commenced the Swachhata Hi Seva Campaign 2026 today. The campaign will continue until 2nd October 2026, reaffirming the Department's commitment to cleanliness and collective public participation.

On the occasion, the Secretary, Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri Sudhansh Pant administered the Swachhata Pledge to officers and officials of all ranks of the Department while other officials took the pledge at their respective seats and offices. The officers and officials posted at other locations also participated from their respective workplaces.

The Organisations under the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment had been directed to organize the Swachhata Pledge at their stationed offices, ensuring wider participation in the campaign across the Department and its institutions.

Through the pledge, participants committed themselves to cleanliness, to devoting 100 hours every year - two hours every week - to voluntary cleanliness work, and to neither litter nor allow others to litter. They also resolved to begin the pursuit of cleanliness with themselves, their families, localities, villages and workplaces, and to encourage others to contribute to the Swachh Bharat Mission.

The observance highlighted that sustained individual action and community participation are central to building clean workplaces, neighbourhoods, villages, towns and a cleaner nation.

headline: Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya Calls for Collective Efforts to Advance Social Justice for a Sustainable Future
fullText:
Ministry of Labour & Employment

Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya Calls for Collective Efforts to Advance Social Justice for a Sustainable Future

Economic Growth and Social Progress Must Move Together: Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya at the Global Coalition for Social Justice Annual Forum 2026

Union Minister Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya Sets Out Three Priorities for the Global Coalition for Social Justice

Global Coalition for Social Justice Annual Forum 2026 Brings Together Global Partners to Advance Social Justice and Decent Work; India Takes Over Co-Chairmanship

17 SEP 2026 1:59PM by PIB Delhi

The Global Coalition for Social Justice Annual Forum 2026 is being held virtually on 16–17 September 2026, bringing together governments, employers’ and workers’ organisations, international and regional organisations, development institutions, the private sector, academia and civil society to strengthen cooperation and accelerate collective action for social justice and decent work. The Official Opening of the Forum was graced by Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya, Union Minister for Labour & Employment and Youth Affairs & Sports, Mr. Gilbert F. Houngbo, Director-General, International Labour Organization (ILO), Ms Jacqueline Mugo, President, International Organisation of Employers; Mr Luc Triangle, General Secretary, International Trade Union Confederation and Mr Luiz Marinho, Minister of Labour and Employment, Brazil.

Addressing the gathering, Union Minister, Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya, called for collective efforts to place social justice at the heart of endeavours, in order to build a more inclusive, resilient and sustainable future. The shared objective of the global community, the Minister said, should be to translate cooperation into opportunities, growth into shared prosperity and commitments to social justice into tangible change. He said India brings to the Forum its experience of delivering transformation at scale and its commitment to building a more inclusive world of work. Emphasising the need for economic growth and social progress to move together, the Minister said that growth must create decent jobs, technology must promote inclusion and innovation must contribute to improving people’s lives.

Dr. Mandaviya said that India is preparing for the future of work through technology, skills and international cooperation. He underlined that the changing world of work requires renewed focus on skills, employability and labour mobility. In this context, he highlighted India’s partnership with the ILO to pilot an International Reference Classification of Occupations across India, Brazil and Germany to support smoother international mobility. He also referred to the New Delhi Declaration 2026 adopted under India’s BRICS Presidency and the BRICS CONNECT initiative, as well as the consensus on an International Digital Platform for Remote Employment to create new virtual employment opportunities for youth across the Global South.

Highlighting India’s reform-led approach, the Minister said that the country continues to focus on transformative reforms, targeted welfare and digital innovation, ensuring that the benefits of economic growth reach the last mile. He drew attention to the consolidation of 29 central labour laws into four modern Labour Codes, stating that the reforms strengthen workers’ protection while creating an enabling environment for enterprises. He also noted that India has become one of the leading countries to provide legal recognition to gig and platform workers. Dr. Mandaviya further emphasised the role of sustained reforms and digital delivery in expanding social protection, noting that India’s social protection coverage has increased from 19 per cent in 2015 to 68.4 per cent in 2026, bringing more than one billion people within the social protection framework.

The Minister highlighted the role of Digital Public Infrastructure in strengthening social protection delivery. He said that the e-Shram portal, with nearly 320 million registered unorganised workers, is the world’s largest digital database of its kind and connects workers with welfare schemes across national and State Governments. Referring to the National Career Service (NCS), he said that the platform connects jobseekers with domestic and international opportunities, with India also sharing the NCS framework with Mauritius.

Dr. Mandaviya said that India stands ready to deepen partnerships across the Global South in areas including digital public infrastructure, social protection, skills and employment services. He said that sharing successful experiences can help translate national achievements into shared progress and reiterated India’s commitment to strengthening the voice of South-South Cooperation in shaping the future of work and advancing social justice. He also noted that as India assumes the Co-Chairmanship of the Coalition’s Coordinating Group, it would build on the leadership provided by Brazil during the important phase of the Coalition.

As Co-Chair, Dr. Mandaviya outlined three priorities for the Coalition. First, he called for translating collective commitments into action at the country level, in line with national priorities and circumstances. Second, he emphasised the need to strengthen knowledge and experience sharing, intensify cooperation and bring more enterprises into the social justice agenda. Third, he stressed that social justice should inform the choices that shape development beyond 2030. He said that with more than 400 partners, the Coalition has unique collective strength, while its objective should not be to prescribe one pathway for all, but to ensure that social justice remains an integral part of the choices countries make about their future.

Dr. Mandaviya reaffirmed India’s commitment to working with all members to make the Global Coalition for Social Justice a strong platform for international cooperation, shared learning and practical action.

The Global Coalition for Social Justice, established by ILO in 2023, is a global platform aimed at strengthening multistakeholder cooperation and accelerating collective action for decent work and social justice. With more than 400 partners comprising governments, employers’ and workers’ organisations, international and regional organisations, development banks, the private sector, academia and civil society, the Coalition seeks to promote coherent and integrated approaches to advance social justice, expand opportunities, foster shared prosperity and contribute to resilient societies.

The Global Coalition for Social Justice Annual Forum 2026 is being held virtually on 16–17 September 2026, ahead of the High-Level General Debate of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly. The Forum provides a platform for partners to share experiences and lessons learned, review progress, identify opportunities for collaboration and shape future collective action.
